introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K. Relative atomic masses: H = 1, C = 12, O = 16, Cl = 35.5, Ag = 108.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the following table (the blank cells are to be filled in by the candidate).

| Test procedure | Observation | Inference or conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| a(i) ................ | Golden colour flame observed with A | ................ |
| (ii) A few drops of dilute HCl are added to solid A in a test tube | A gas is evolved with a smell like that of burning match | ................ |

*[(i) 3 marks; (ii) 2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Test procedure (flame test):** dip a clean nichrome (or platinum) wire in concentrated hydrochloric acid, then into solid **A** (or moisten the wire with acid and touch the salt), and hold it in the **non-luminous (blue) Bunsen flame**. **Inference:** the golden-yellow flame shows that **sodium ions, $\mathrm{Na^+}$, are present**.

(ii) **Inference:** the gas with a smell like burning matches is **sulphur dioxide**, $\mathrm{SO_2}$, so **sulphite ions, $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$, are present**:

$\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}} + 2\mathrm{H^+} \rightarrow \mathrm{SO_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$

(The gas turns acidified potassium dichromate(VI) paper from orange to green.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the following table (the blank cells are to be filled in by the candidate).

| Test procedure | Observation | Inference or conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| b(i) To 2 cm$^3$ of solution B is added a few drops of NaOH(aq) | A blue precipitate is formed | ................ |
| (ii) To 2 cm$^3$ of solution B is added $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$ followed by dilute HCl(aq) | ................ | $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ ions present |

*[(i) 1 mark; (ii) 2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Inference:** the blue precipitate is copper(II) hydroxide, so **copper(II) ions, $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$, are present**: $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}} + 2\mathrm{OH^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu(OH)_2}$.

(ii) **Observation:** a **white precipitate** (barium sulphate) forms with barium chloride and **does not dissolve** when dilute hydrochloric acid is added: $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}} + \mathrm{SO_4^{2-}} \rightarrow \mathrm{BaSO_4}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the following table (the blank cells are to be filled in by the candidate).

| Test procedure | Observation | Inference or conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| c(i) Add NaOH(aq) to solution C and test with a litmus paper | ................ | $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ ions present |
| (ii) To 2 cm$^3$ of solution C is added acidified $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$(aq) | White precipitate is formed | ................ |

*[(i) 2 marks; (ii) 1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Observation:** on warming, a **colourless gas with a pungent smell** (ammonia) is given off, and it **turns damp red litmus paper blue**: $\mathrm{NH_4^+} + \mathrm{OH^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{NH_3} + \mathrm{H_2O}$.

(ii) **Inference:** the white precipitate is silver chloride, so **chloride ions, $\mathrm{Cl^-}$, are present**: $\mathrm{Ag^+} + \mathrm{Cl^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{AgCl}$.

- **A** contains $\mathrm{Na^+}$ and $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$: **sodium sulphite**, $\mathrm{Na_2SO_3}$.
- **B** contains $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$: **copper(II) sulphate**, $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$.
- **C** contains $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$: **ammonium chloride**, $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the following table by identifying the method of collection.

| Gas | Draw or state the method of collection |
|---|---|
| Ammonia ($\mathrm{NH_3}$) | |
| Sulphur dioxide ($\mathrm{SO_2}$) | |
| Hydrogen ($\mathrm{H_2}$) | |

*[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Gas | Method of collection | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Ammonia ($\mathrm{NH_3}$) | **Upward delivery** (downward displacement of air): gas jar held upside down | less dense than air and very soluble in water |
| Sulphur dioxide ($\mathrm{SO_2}$) | **Downward delivery** (upward displacement of air): gas jar upright | denser than air and soluble in water |
| Hydrogen ($\mathrm{H_2}$) | **Over water** (downward displacement of water); upward delivery of air is also acceptable | insoluble in water and less dense than air |

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following data was recorded during the preparation of a standard solution of sodium carbonate.

Mass of empty bottle = 5.56 g

Mass of bottle plus salt = 16.10 g

Calculate the mass of the salt weighed and the amount of substance in mol. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Mass of the salt weighed** = mass of bottle plus salt - mass of empty bottle = $16.10 - 5.56 =$ **10.54 g**

**Amount of substance in mol:**

Molar mass of $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ = $2 \times 23 + 12 + 3 \times 16 = 106$ g/mol

Amount = $\dfrac{\text{mass}}{\text{molar mass}} = \dfrac{10.54}{106} =$ **0.0994 mol** ($\approx 0.099$ mol)
